## Purpose and entry points
Metaflow is a Python-first framework for authoring, executing, tracking, and deploying AI/ML workflows (“flows”) from local development through cloud-scale production. The public runtime is the `metaflow` package; command invocation is centered on `metaflow/cli.py` and `metaflow/cmd/main_cli.py`. Users define flows by subclassing `FlowSpec` and marking step methods, primarily through `metaflow/flowspec.py`, `metaflow/decorators.py`, and `metaflow/parameters.py`.

## Flow definition, graph inference, and execution
A flow’s step methods and `self.next()` transitions are converted into a DAG, including branches, `foreach`, parallelism, and switches. `metaflow/graph.py` models/inferes graph structure; `metaflow/runtime.py` schedules local task execution; `metaflow/task.py` executes an individual step/task. This is the core control boundary: user flow code is interpreted as a graph, then each graph node becomes an isolated task execution.

## CLI and programmatic orchestration
The CLI exposes flow lifecycle commands such as run, resume, dump, and step execution via `metaflow/cli_components/run_cmds.py`, `metaflow/cli_components/step_cmd.py`, and `metaflow/cli_components/dump_cmd.py`. The Python Runner API launches and manages flows as subprocesses through `metaflow/runner/metaflow_runner.py` and `metaflow/runner/subprocess_manager.py`. These layers translate user commands/API calls into runtime task invocations and backend-specific operations.

## Artifacts, metadata, and client access
Tasks persist artifacts, code/package references, logs, and lineage separately from execution control. The datastore abstraction and task-level persistence reside in `metaflow/datastore/flow_datastore.py`, `metaflow/datastore/task_datastore.py`, and `metaflow/datastore/content_addressed_store.py`; artifact serialization is handled under `metaflow/datastore/artifacts/serializer.py`. Metadata is supplied through configurable providers in `metaflow/metadata_provider/metadata.py` and `metaflow/plugins/metadata_providers/service.py`. The read-side client API navigates flows, runs, steps, tasks, and artifacts through `metaflow/client/core.py`.

## Extensible execution and deployment backends
Decorators annotate flows/steps with execution requirements and behavior; plugin discovery makes backends replaceable or additive. Core extension mechanisms are in `metaflow/decorators.py`, `metaflow/extension_support/plugins.py`, and `metaflow/plugins/__init__.py`. Material compute/deployment targets include AWS Batch (`metaflow/plugins/aws/batch/batch.py`), Kubernetes (`metaflow/plugins/kubernetes/kubernetes.py`), Argo Workflows (`metaflow/plugins/argo/argo_workflows.py`), Airflow (`metaflow/plugins/airflow/airflow.py`), and AWS Step Functions (`metaflow/plugins/aws/step_functions/step_functions.py`).

## Cloud services, environments, and observability
Datastore adapters support local files, Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, and Google Cloud Storage via `metaflow/plugins/datastores/local_storage.py`, `metaflow/plugins/datastores/s3_storage.py`, and `metaflow/plugins/datastores/azure_storage.py`. Dependency environments are provisioned by PyPI/Conda and uv plugins in `metaflow/plugins/pypi/pypi_environment.py` and `metaflow/plugins/uv/uv_environment.py`. Runtime logging, monitoring, tracing, and sidecars are separated from user tasks in `metaflow/mflog/mflog.py`, `metaflow/tracing/propagator.py`, and `metaflow/sidecar/sidecar.py`.

## Presentation and language bindings
Cards render task/run results into portable visual artifacts and can be served/viewed through `metaflow/plugins/cards/card_creator.py`, `metaflow/plugins/cards/card_server.py`, and the Svelte UI at `metaflow/plugins/cards/ui/src/App.svelte`. The repository also ships an R package binding that constructs and controls Metaflow flows through `R/R/flow.R`, `R/R/step.R`, and `R/inst/run.R`, bridging R-authored workflows to the Python runtime.
